note: Written player bios and value drivers. Career facts as of 2025-26; live signals are computed on the page.

lebron-james.bio: The NBA's all-time leading scorer and the first player to pass 40,000 points. Four titles and four MVPs across a career that started straight out of high school in 2003.
drivers: Every hint about his final season pushes collectors to buy before the farewell tour.
Scoring records and playing alongside his son Bronny bring short bursts of demand.
His 2003-04 rookie cards are treated like long-term investments, so they hold value even in slow markets.

stephen-curry.bio: The greatest shooter in NBA history and the all-time leader in made threes. Four titles, two MVPs (one unanimous) and a 2022 Finals MVP.
drivers: Three-point milestones and big scoring nights get attention fast.
His prices follow how far the team goes in the postseason.
As he nears the end of his career, legacy buying keeps a floor under his 2009-10 rookies.

kevin-durant.bio: One of the most efficient scorers ever, with two titles, two Finals MVPs, a 2014 MVP and a record four Olympic gold medals.
drivers: He came back from a 2019 Achilles tear, so any injury news moves his cards more than usual.
Trades and new teams reset the story around him and often bring a bump.
Climbing the all-time scoring list keeps legacy collectors interested.

giannis-antetokounmpo.bio: A two-time MVP, 2020 Defensive Player of the Year and 2021 champion and Finals MVP. Drafted 15th as a raw 18-year-old from Greece.
drivers: Talk about him leaving Milwaukee is one of the biggest swings in the NBA card market.
Deep runs bring back the 2021 title story and lift prices.
His rise from a late lottery pick makes his 2013-14 rookies a favorite with long-term holders.

nikola-jokic.bio: A three-time MVP and the 2023 champion and Finals MVP. He went 41st overall in 2014, one of the biggest draft steals ever.
drivers: His prices rise and fall with the MVP voting conversation.
Stat-sheet records and historic nights draw attention.
As a second-round pick he had fewer premium rookie cards made, so the good ones are scarce.

luka-doncic.bio: The 2019 Rookie of the Year and a perennial MVP candidate who led Dallas to the 2024 Finals. A stunning 2025 trade sent him to the Lakers.
drivers: Joining the Lakers widened his fan base and the number of buyers.
Questions about fitness and minor injuries cause quick dips.
50-point games and MVP talk bring sharp short-term spikes.

joel-embiid.bio: The 2023 MVP and a two-time scoring champion. He missed his first two seasons with foot injuries after going third in 2014.
drivers: Availability is the single biggest factor. Injury news hits his cards hard.
Early exits weigh on his market more than regular-season numbers help it.
A healthy stretch can bring big percentage gains from a lower base.

jayson-tatum.bio: The third pick in 2017 and the leader of Boston's 2024 title team. A multi-time All-NBA first-teamer.
drivers: He tore his Achilles in the 2025 playoffs, so return-to-play news is the main driver right now.
The 2024 title keeps his graded rookies in steady demand.
Boston has a large, active collector base.

anthony-edwards.bio: The first pick in 2020, a 2024 Olympic gold medalist and the face of Minnesota's back-to-back conference finals runs.
drivers: Big commercials and highlight dunks keep him in the spotlight.
Deep postseason runs have produced his biggest price jumps.
Collectors buy him as a long-term bet on the league's next superstar.

shai-gilgeous-alexander.bio: The 2025 MVP, 2025 champion and Finals MVP. He turned into the league's top scorer after going 11th in 2018.
drivers: Defending the title and MVP keeps demand high; a slip would cool it.
Many collectors were late to him, so his market is still catching up.

victor-wembanyama.bio: The first pick in 2023 and the 2024 Rookie of the Year, a 7-foot-4 talent who led the league in blocks as a rookie.
drivers: A blood clot ended his 2024-25 season early. Health news is the biggest swing factor.
He's priced like a future MVP, so big games move him a lot and quiet stretches cool him.
His 2023-24 rookies are some of the most traded modern basketball cards.

ja-morant.bio: The second pick in 2019, Rookie of the Year and 2022 Most Improved Player. Known for some of the most explosive dunks in the league.
drivers: League suspensions in 2023 hit his cards hard. Headlines still move them.
Shoulder and other injuries have cost him big stretches.
Viral dunks bring short bursts of buying.

zion-williamson.bio: The first pick in 2019 after one of the most hyped college seasons ever at Duke.
drivers: Missed games have been the main story, so health is everything for his cards.
Prices are well below his rookie peak, so healthy stretches bring big percentage gains.
A new team could reset his market.

devin-booker.bio: A four-time All-Star who scored 70 in a game at age 20, led Phoenix to the 2021 Finals and won Olympic gold in 2024.
drivers: His cards follow Phoenix's results more than his own scoring.
Big nights remind collectors of his 70-point game.
A deep fan base keeps prices from falling far.

jalen-brunson.bio: The Knicks captain and 2025 Clutch Player of the Year, a second-round pick in 2018 who became a top-10 scorer.
drivers: Knicks success brings one of the biggest fan bases into the hobby.
Postseason performances drive his largest moves.
Lower print runs from his quiet rookie year make good copies scarce.

tyrese-haliburton.bio: Indiana's All-NBA point guard who led the Pacers to the 2025 Finals with a string of game-winning shots.
drivers: He tore his Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals, so recovery news is the main driver.
His 2025 playoff run created a lasting story collectors pay for.
Indiana's smaller fan base limits how high prices go.

paolo-banchero.bio: The first pick in 2022 and the 2023 Rookie of the Year, Orlando's lead scorer.
drivers: Talk of a jump to superstar level brings buying.
Orlando's playoff success lifts his profile.
Missed time cools his market quickly.

chet-holmgren.bio: The second pick in 2022 who missed his first season with a foot injury, then won a title with Oklahoma City in 2025.
drivers: The 2025 title gave his cards a lasting boost.
His thin frame makes injury news a bigger concern for buyers.
His prices react when his role on the team grows or shrinks.

cade-cunningham.bio: The first pick in 2021 who turned Detroit around and led the Pistons back to the playoffs in 2025.
drivers: Detroit winning is the main reason his cards have climbed.
Awards confirm he's a star and support prices.
Buyers see room to grow, so good months bring strong gains.

lamelo-ball.bio: The third pick in 2020 and the 2021 Rookie of the Year, known for flashy passing and long-range shooting.
drivers: Repeated ankle problems have kept prices down.
His family name and big social following bring in buyers outside the usual hobby.
Strong runs of games bring quick rebounds.

donovan-mitchell.bio: A multi-time All-Star scoring guard who scored 71 in a 2023 game and leads Cleveland's contender.
drivers: Getting past the second round is the story that would lift his cards most.
His rookies sit below the top stars, so they move with the overall market.

kawhi-leonard.bio: A two-time champion and two-time Finals MVP with two different teams, plus two Defensive Player of the Year awards.
drivers: Managed minutes and knee issues make availability the main factor.
His past playoff runs keep a strong base of buyers.
League investigations or team news can cause sharp moves.

damian-lillard.bio: The 2013 Rookie of the Year and a nine-time All-Star known for long-range game-winners.
drivers: He tore his Achilles in the 2025 playoffs, so recovery news drives his market.
His history in Portland keeps a loyal set of collectors.
Hall of Fame talk supports his 2012-13 rookies.

anthony-davis.bio: The first pick in 2012, a 2020 champion and a perennial All-NBA big man. He was traded to Dallas in the 2025 Luka trade.
drivers: Injuries have been the steady drag on his prices.
His new team's success after the 2025 trade drives his market.
Hall of Fame odds support older graded rookies.

cooper-flagg.bio: The first pick in the 2025 draft after winning national player of the year as a Duke freshman.
drivers: Every early game is scored by collectors. Big nights cause sharp jumps, slumps cause sharp drops.
Award odds are a direct driver this season.
His NBA rookies come as Topps returns to basketball, which brings new sets and heavy print-run attention.

dylan-harper.bio: The second pick in the 2025 draft after a standout freshman season at Rutgers.
drivers: How much he plays as a rookie is the biggest driver right now.
Early-career cards swing harder in both directions than established stars.

michael-jordan.bio: Widely seen as the greatest basketball player ever. Six titles, six Finals MVPs and five MVPs.
drivers: His 1986-87 Fleer rookie is one of the most traded cards in the hobby, so it sets the tone for his whole market.
Media like The Last Dance have caused big jumps.
As a blue-chip name, he moves with the broad card market.

kobe-bryant.bio: A five-time champion, 2008 MVP and author of the 81-point game. He died in a helicopter crash in 2020.
drivers: Dates tied to his career and life bring waves of buying.
His 1996-97 rookies, especially Topps Chrome, are hobby staples.
High-grade copies of his rookies are hard to find, which supports PSA 10 prices.

tim-duncan.bio: A five-time champion, two-time MVP and three-time Finals MVP, all with San Antonio.
drivers: His quiet personality kept prices lower than his résumé suggests, which draws value buyers.
The Wembanyama era has brought new attention to Spurs legends.
PSA 10 copies of his 1997-98 rookies carry most of the value.

shaquille-oneal.bio: A four-time champion, three-time Finals MVP and 2000 MVP. One of the most dominant centers ever.
drivers: His TV and commercial fame keeps new fans buying.
His rookie year has many sets, so condition and grade matter most.
1990s collectors coming back to the hobby lift his market.

magic-johnson.bio: A five-time champion and three-time MVP whose rivalry with Larry Bird reshaped the NBA in the 1980s.
drivers: His key rookie is the 1980 Topps card he shares with Larry Bird and Julius Erving.
Centering and grade drive huge price differences on 1980s cards.
Showtime Lakers anniversaries and media bring interest.

larry-bird.bio: A three-time champion and three straight MVPs from 1984 to 1986 with Boston.
drivers: His main rookie is the 1980 Topps card with Magic Johnson and Julius Erving.
High grades are rare, so PSA 10s sell at a big premium.
Boston's success brings attention back to its legends.

dirk-nowitzki.bio: The 2007 MVP and 2011 champion and Finals MVP, who spent all 21 seasons with Dallas.
drivers: Hall of Fame recognition and his one-team career keep a steady base.
His popularity in Europe adds buyers beyond the US.
His 1998-99 rookies are limited, which supports graded prices.

dwyane-wade.bio: A three-time champion and the 2006 Finals MVP, one of the best shooting guards ever.
drivers: He's tied to the famous 2003 class with LeBron, so that class's interest helps him.
His high-end 2003-04 rookies drive his top-end market.

allen-iverson.bio: The first pick in 1996, 2001 MVP and four-time scoring champion. A cultural icon of his era.
drivers: His style and influence on fashion and hip-hop bring in collectors beyond basketball.
He's part of a famous class with Kobe, which keeps attention high.
Clean high-grade copies are hard to find.

kevin-garnett.bio: The 2004 MVP, 2008 champion and Defensive Player of the Year, drafted straight out of high school in 1995.
drivers: His prices sit below other legends of his era, drawing value buyers.
His media presence keeps him in front of fans.
PSA 10 1995-96 rookies drive most of his value.

shohei-ohtani.bio: Baseball's two-way superstar who hits like an MVP and pitches like an ace. Multiple MVPs, the first 50-homer, 50-steal season in 2024 and back-to-back World Series titles with the Dodgers.
drivers: Starts on the mound add to his value because they show the two-way story is still going.
Collectors in Japan and the US compete for his cards, which keeps prices high.
Records and milestone games cause quick spikes.

mike-trout.bio: A three-time AL MVP and one of the best players of his generation, whose recent seasons have been cut short by injuries.
drivers: Time on the injured list has been the biggest drag on his market.
His 2009 Bowman Chrome prospect autograph is the hobby's benchmark modern baseball card.
A healthy, productive year could bring a strong rebound.

aaron-judge.bio: The Yankees captain who set the AL record with 62 homers in 2022 and has won multiple AL MVPs.
drivers: His prices track his home run totals during the season.
New York's huge fan base gives him deep demand.
October performances, good or bad, move his cards sharply.

juan-soto.bio: A patient, powerful hitter who won the 2019 World Series at age 20 and later signed a record contract with the Mets.
drivers: His huge deal raised expectations, so slumps get noticed fast.
Playing in New York brings big attention and big swings.
His early-career numbers compare to all-time greats, which supports long-term buying.

ronald-acuna-jr.bio: The 2023 NL MVP and the first player with 40 homers and 70 steals in a season.
drivers: Two torn ACLs make his health the biggest factor.
Speed and power highlights bring quick buying.
A strong return season would bring a big rebound.

fernando-tatis-jr.bio: An electric outfielder who signed a long extension with San Diego early in his career.
drivers: A 2022 PED suspension hurt his market. Clean, strong seasons help repair it.
Big homers and defensive plays bring short bursts.
His 2019 rookies and prospect autos are heavily traded.

bobby-witt-jr.bio: Kansas City's star shortstop, the second pick in 2019 and the 2024 AL batting champion.
drivers: Being in the MVP conversation is his biggest driver.
Speed, power and defense keep him in the spotlight all season.
Kansas City's smaller fan base keeps prices below big-city stars.

julio-rodriguez.bio: Seattle's center fielder and the 2022 AL Rookie of the Year.
drivers: He often starts seasons cold and finishes hot, so prices swing within a season.
His personality and highlights bring in younger collectors.
Mariners playoff runs lift his profile.

gunnar-henderson.bio: Baltimore's star shortstop and the 2023 AL Rookie of the Year.
drivers: Home run totals for a shortstop drive interest.
He's the face of a young Orioles team, so team success matters.

elly-de-la-cruz.bio: Cincinnati's switch-hitting shortstop with rare speed and arm strength.
drivers: Moon-shot homers, steals and throws bring sudden spikes.
Long slumps lead to quick drops, so his market is volatile.
Buyers are paying for a very high upside.

corbin-carroll.bio: Arizona's outfielder and the unanimous 2023 NL Rookie of the Year.
drivers: His stats have varied year to year, and prices follow.
Stolen base totals help his profile.
Arizona's fan base limits the top end.

paul-skenes.bio: The first pick in 2023, the 2024 NL Rookie of the Year and the 2025 NL Cy Young winner.
drivers: Pitchers' cards react to each outing, so his prices swing week to week.
Any elbow or shoulder news is a major risk for pitcher cards.
A move to a bigger market or contender would widen demand.

jackson-holliday.bio: The first pick in 2022 and once baseball's top prospect, son of former All-Star Matt Holliday.
drivers: His early major league struggles cut prices. Signs of a breakout would bring a big rebound.
His Bowman prospect autos drove most of his early value.
Playing time and batting order matter a lot right now.

jackson-chourio.bio: Milwaukee's young outfielder who became one of the youngest players ever with a 20-20 season as a rookie in 2024.
drivers: Being so young means buyers see a lot of growth ahead.
Home run and steal totals drive interest.
Milwaukee's fan base keeps prices lower.

wyatt-langford.bio: Texas's outfielder, the fourth pick in 2023, who reached the majors within a year.
drivers: Collectors are waiting for a big season, so hot stretches move him quickly.
Missed time has slowed his market.
His Bowman autos carry much of the value.

roman-anthony.bio: Boston's top prospect who debuted in 2025 and quickly signed a long-term extension.
drivers: His first full season is what collectors are watching.
Boston's large fan base brings strong demand.
His Bowman Chrome autos are the main high-end cards.

mookie-betts.bio: The 2018 AL MVP and a multi-time World Series champion with Boston and the Dodgers.
drivers: Titles keep his Hall of Fame case growing.
His moves around the field get attention but rarely move prices much.
His rookies trade steadily with fewer big swings.

bryce-harper.bio: The first pick in 2010 and a two-time NL MVP, now Philadelphia's first baseman.
drivers: Playoff runs bring his biggest moves.
His 2011 Bowman prospect cards are classics.

vladimir-guerrero-jr.bio: Toronto's slugging first baseman and son of a Hall of Famer, who signed a huge extension in 2025.
drivers: Staying in Toronto settled his future and steadied his market.
As Canada's biggest baseball star he has a dedicated buying base.
Home run totals drive his yearly swings.

francisco-lindor.bio: The Mets' star shortstop and team captain.
drivers: Strong seasons near the top of MVP voting lift prices.
His 2015 rookies are affordable and move with team results.

pete-alonso.bio: A slugging first baseman who hit a rookie-record 53 homers in 2019 and became the Mets' all-time home run leader.
drivers: His cards follow his power numbers.
Free agency and team changes move his market.
Strong fan loyalty supports a steady base.

yoshinobu-yamamoto.bio: A Japanese ace who signed with the Dodgers and won World Series MVP in 2025.
drivers: His 2025 World Series performance lifted his market.
Japanese and US collectors both buy his cards.
Arm injury news is the biggest risk.

clayton-kershaw.bio: A three-time Cy Young winner and 2014 NL MVP who spent his whole career with the Dodgers and retired after the 2025 season.
drivers: Now retired, his cards move with Hall of Fame news.
His 3,000th strikeout and title wins anchor his legacy.

ken-griffey-jr.bio: A Hall of Famer with 630 homers and 10 Gold Gloves, one of the most loved players of the 1990s.
drivers: His 1989 Upper Deck #1 is one of the hobby's most famous cards.
Collectors who grew up in the 1990s drive his market.
PSA 10 copies sell for many times the price of lower grades.

derek-jeter.bio: The Yankees captain with five World Series titles and more than 3,400 hits, inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2020.
drivers: The huge Yankees fan base keeps demand steady.
His 1993 SP rookie is famously hard to find in high grade.
Career milestones and anniversaries bring buying.

mickey-mantle.bio: A Yankees legend with seven World Series titles and three MVPs, inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1974.
drivers: A 1952 Topps Mantle sold for $12.6 million in 2022, and record sales lift his whole market.
Grade drives huge price differences on 1950s cards.
As a blue-chip name, he moves with the broad market.

hank-aaron.bio: Baseball's home run king for 33 years with 755 homers. He died in 2021.
drivers: Anniversaries and tributes bring waves of interest.
His 1954 Topps rookie is a vintage staple.
High grades are rare and sell at a premium.

willie-mays.bio: The Say Hey Kid, with 660 homers and 12 Gold Gloves. He died in June 2024.
drivers: Prices rose after his death and have since settled.
His 1951 Bowman rookie is one of the key vintage cards.
Grade drives most of the value.

roberto-clemente.bio: A Hall of Famer with 3,000 hits, 12 Gold Gloves and a humanitarian legacy. He died in a 1972 plane crash on a relief mission.
drivers: His annual day and anniversaries bring renewed interest.
His 1955 Topps rookie is a vintage staple.
Strong demand from fans across Latin America.

nolan-ryan.bio: The all-time strikeout leader with 5,714 and a record seven no-hitters.
drivers: His 1968 Topps rookie, shared with Jerry Koosman, carries most of his value.
Off-center copies are common, so well-centered high grades sell at big premiums.

cal-ripken-jr.bio: Baseball's Iron Man, who played 2,632 straight games, with two MVPs and 3,000 hits.
drivers: His 1982 Topps Traded rookie is the key card.
His market moves slowly and steadily.

albert-pujols.bio: A three-time MVP with 703 home runs, two World Series titles and more than 3,000 hits.
drivers: His Hall of Fame election, likely on the first ballot, should bring a bump.
His 2001 Bowman Chrome and Topps Chrome rookies are the key cards.

ichiro-suzuki.bio: The 2001 AL MVP and Rookie of the Year, with the single-season hits record of 262 and 3,000 MLB hits. Inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2025.
drivers: Collectors in Japan and the US both buy.
His 2001 rookies, especially high grades, carry the value.

mariano-rivera.bio: The all-time saves leader with 652 and the first unanimous Hall of Fame selection.
drivers: His 1992 Bowman rookie is the key card.

babe-ruth.bio: Baseball's first great slugger, with 714 homers and seven World Series titles.
drivers: Few high-grade cards survive, so every big sale sets a new benchmark.
Record sales of game-used items or cards lift his whole market.
Grading and authentication matter more than usual.

patrick-mahomes.bio: A three-time Super Bowl champion and two-time MVP who redefined quarterback play.
drivers: His cards follow how far the Chiefs go in January.
Passing milestones keep him in the spotlight.
His 2017 rookies are seen as the top modern football cards.

josh-allen.bio: Buffalo's dual-threat quarterback and the 2024 MVP, the seventh pick in 2018.
drivers: A Super Bowl run would be the biggest driver.
Big runs and throws bring short spikes.

joe-burrow.bio: Cincinnati's quarterback, the 2019 Heisman winner and first pick in 2020, who led the Bengals to Super Bowl LVI.
drivers: Multiple major injuries make his availability the biggest factor.
Postseason wins drive his biggest gains.
His 2020 class is strong, which helps interest.

lamar-jackson.bio: Baltimore's quarterback and a two-time MVP, the last pick of the first round in 2018.
drivers: Postseason wins matter most to his market.

justin-herbert.bio: The Chargers' quarterback, sixth pick in 2020 and Offensive Rookie of the Year.
drivers: A deep run would bring the biggest boost.
Strong passing numbers keep steady interest.
Los Angeles fan base gives moderate demand.

cj-stroud.bio: Houston's quarterback, second pick in 2023 and Offensive Rookie of the Year.
drivers: His second season dipped, so a strong year could bring a rebound.
Young quarterbacks get extra hobby attention.

caleb-williams.bio: Chicago's quarterback, first pick in 2024 and 2022 Heisman winner.
drivers: His progress in Chicago is the main driver.
Chicago's large fan base widens demand.

jayden-daniels.bio: Washington's quarterback, second pick in 2024, 2023 Heisman winner and 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year.
drivers: His running style makes injury news important.
His rookie NFC title game run raised expectations.
Strong demand for top young quarterbacks.

drake-maye.bio: New England's quarterback, third pick in 2024.
drivers: Signs of a breakout drive his market.
A strong New England fan base.

bo-nix.bio: Denver's quarterback, 12th pick in 2024, who led the Broncos to the playoffs as a rookie.
drivers: His later draft slot means wins surprise collectors in a good way.

brock-purdy.bio: San Francisco's quarterback, the final pick of the 2022 draft, who led the 49ers to Super Bowl LVIII.
drivers: Mr. Irrelevant to Super Bowl starter makes a story collectors like.
Few premium rookies were made for a last-round pick.

jalen-hurts.bio: Philadelphia's quarterback and Super Bowl LIX MVP, a second-round pick in 2020.
drivers: His Super Bowl win lifted his market.

justin-jefferson.bio: Minnesota's star receiver, 2022 Offensive Player of the Year.
drivers: Receiver cards depend on who's throwing to him.

jamarr-chase.bio: Cincinnati's star receiver, fifth pick in 2021, who won the receiving triple crown in 2024.
drivers: His value is tied to Burrow's health.
Yardage and touchdown totals drive interest.
Dallas's huge fan base brings deep demand.
His numbers depend on the quarterback situation.
Postseason struggles have held his market back.

tyreek-hill.bio: One of the fastest players in NFL history and a multiple All-Pro receiver.
drivers: Receivers in their 30s tend to see declining prices.
Headlines can move his cards sharply.

travis-kelce.bio: A three-time Super Bowl champion and one of the best tight ends ever.
drivers: His relationship with Taylor Swift brought in new buyers outside the hobby.
Talk of retirement brings legacy buying.

christian-mccaffrey.bio: San Francisco's star running back and the 2023 Offensive Player of the Year.
drivers: Injuries are the biggest factor for running backs.
Running backs decline earlier, which weighs on prices.
His touches per game drive interest.

saquon-barkley.bio: Philadelphia's running back, who ran for over 2,000 yards in 2024 and won a Super Bowl.
drivers: Running back age curves weigh on long-term prices.

bijan-robinson.bio: Atlanta's star running back, eighth pick in 2023.
drivers: Running back primes are short, so buyers move early.

puka-nacua.bio: A fifth-round pick who set the NFL rookie record for receiving yards in 2023.
drivers: Low draft slot means few premium rookies, which helps scarcity.
His quarterback situation affects his numbers.

malik-nabers.bio: The Giants' star receiver, sixth pick in 2024.
drivers: A big fan base supports demand.

marvin-harrison-jr.bio: Arizona's receiver, fourth pick in 2024, son of a Hall of Famer.
drivers: A big season would bring a rebound.
His father's Hall of Fame career adds interest.
He held out of some trading card deals early, which affected his card supply.

brock-bowers.bio: Las Vegas's tight end, 13th pick in 2024, who set the rookie tight end receptions record.
drivers: Tight end cards usually sell below QBs and WRs.
Early performance is the biggest driver.

travis-hunter.bio: A two-way star, 2024 Heisman winner and second pick in 2025.
drivers: Whether he plays both ways drives his story.
His unique role brings heavy demand.

ashton-jeanty.bio: A running back who ran for 2,601 yards at Boise State in 2024 and was the sixth pick in 2025.
drivers: Short primes make buyers act early.

shedeur-sanders.bio: A quarterback who fell to the fifth round in 2025, son of Deion Sanders.
drivers: His name and fan base bring heavy demand despite his draft slot.
Starts and playing time are the biggest driver.
His cards swing hard on news.

aaron-rodgers.bio: A four-time MVP and Super Bowl XLV champion, one of the most accurate passers ever.
drivers: Talk of retirement brings legacy buying.
His 2023 Achilles tear reminds buyers of age risk.
Long-term value tied to his Hall of Fame case.

tom-brady.bio: A seven-time Super Bowl champion and five-time Super Bowl MVP, widely seen as the greatest quarterback ever.
drivers: His 2000 Playoff Contenders auto is a hobby benchmark.
His broadcasting career keeps him visible.
His induction is expected to bring a bump.

peyton-manning.bio: A five-time MVP and two-time Super Bowl champion, first pick in 1998.
drivers: His TV work keeps him visible.

jerry-rice.bio: The NFL's all-time leader in receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns.
drivers: His 1986 Topps rookie is the key card.
Clean copies are hard to find.

joe-montana.bio: A four-time Super Bowl champion and three-time Super Bowl MVP.
drivers: His 1981 Topps rookie is the key card.

walter-payton.bio: One of the greatest running backs ever. He retired as the NFL's all-time rushing leader and died in 1999.
drivers: His 1976 Topps rookie is a vintage staple.
Grade drives most of the value.

barry-sanders.bio: One of the most elusive runners ever, who retired suddenly in 1999 near his peak.
drivers: His 1989 Score rookie is the key card.
Detroit's recent success brings attention to its legends.

emmitt-smith.bio: The NFL's all-time rushing leader and a three-time Super Bowl champion with Dallas.
drivers: A huge fan base supports prices.
His 1990 rookies are the key cards.
His rushing record keeps his legacy strong.
